chunks: And with this chain, from Sulaiman ad-Dailami, from Abu Bassir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I am the Shepherd, the Shepherd of all people. Is it acceptable that a shepherd does not know his sheep?' He said: 'Then Juwairiya stood up and asked: O Amir al-Mu'minin, who are your sheep?' He (peace be upon him) answered: 'Those with pale faces and dry lips due to the remembrance of Allah.'

key_terms.ذَبِلَ الشَّفَاهِ: Dry lips (from lack of food/water due to devotion)

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'sheep' of Imam Ali according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Fadail al-Shia*, Imam Ali (as) employs the pastoral metaphor of the shepherd to define his spiritual guardianship, identifying his 'flock' not by status but by the physical signs of asceticism—pale faces and chapped lips resulting from intense *dhikr*. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the tangible effects of devotion in the righteous, linking leadership directly to spiritual humility and constant remembrance of the Divine.

en.badr-shahin: (The same previous series of relaters)… from Sulaiman ad-Dailami related from Abu Bassir from Abu Abdullah (a) that

Amir ul-Mu’minin (a) said: "I am the shepherd-the shepherd of people. Is it acceptable that a shepherd does not identify his sheep?" Juwairiya stood up and asked: "O Amir ul-Mu’minin, who are your sheep?" He (a) answered: "My sheep are pale-faced and dry-lipped because of the mention of Allah."
